summary: A best current practice with implementation guidelines for running RSVP over ATM switched virtual circuits.

eli5.summary: Tips for reserving some space on an ATM network for important traffic.

subtitle: Recommended choices for carrying RSVP reservations over ATM virtual circuits so different implementations behave predictably.

tldr.problem: RSVP reservations and ATM switched virtual circuits (SVCs) do not map one to one, and free choices among the options could leave implementations unable to interoperate.
tldr.mechanism: The memo recommends a baseline: send RSVP control messages over the best effort data path, use an independent VC per reservation, let QoS short-cuts follow best effort short-cuts, and implement either the limited heterogeneity or the modified homogeneous model.
tldr.outcome: It is a Best Current Practice companion to the framework and requirements documents, and it raises no new security issues.

today: RFC 2379 is a Best Current Practice (BCP 24), and the metadata for this RFC lists no obsoleting or updating RFC. It is a companion to RFC 2380 and RFC 2382.

sections.title: Scope of the Guidelines
sections.content:
This memo covers running IP over ATM where SVCs (switched virtual circuits) carry QoS flows and RSVP is the internet-level QoS signaling protocol. It applies when using CLIP/ION, LANE2.0 and MPOA methods for IP over ATM, and recommends functionality for implementations using ATM UNI3.x and 4.0.

It is a companion to the framework in RFC 2382 and the requirements in RFC 2380, and the reader should know both. The recommended baseline exists to ensure predictability and interoperability, while allowing more sophisticated approaches that some vendors and networks may adopt. The usual RFC 2119 key words apply.
sections.eli5: RSVP is a way to ask the network to save room for your data, and ATM is a kind of network with private pathways. This memo says how to use the two together.

sections.title: Where RSVP Messages Travel
sections.content:
RSVP over ATM implementations SHOULD send RSVP control messages over the best effort data path, though a user may be allowed to override this. This minimizes VC requirements, because the best effort path must exist anyway for sessions to be established and reservations initiated. For unicast, the path is the same VC used to reach the destination. For multicast, it is the VC used for best effort traffic to the IP multicast group.

The drawback is that best effort VCs may not give the reliability RSVP needs. The memo expects them to be good enough in most networks, especially since RSVP tolerates a certain amount of packet loss without losing state synchronization.
sections.eli5: The little notes that say "please reserve a lane" ride on the ordinary road, not the special lane. The ordinary road is usually good enough.

sections.title: Aggregation
sections.content: Data for several RSVP sessions could in principle share VCs, which is called aggregation. The memo says such models are still a matter for research, so RSVP over ATM implementations SHOULD use independent VCs for each RSVP reservation.
sections.eli5: For now, every reservation gets its own private lane instead of sharing, because sharing is still being figured out.

sections.title: Short-Cuts
sections.content:
Short-cuts let ATM-attached routers and hosts set up point-to-point VCs directly across LIS boundaries, so the endpoints sit on different IP subnets. Unicast short-cuts are defined in RFC 2332 and the ATM Forum's MPOA specification. The worry is asymmetric short-cuts: PATH and RESV messages may follow different paths.

The memo finds that RSVP already copes. RSVP messages are processed only when they arrive at the proper interface, indicated by the NHOP object. Messages that arrive on the wrong interface are forwarded. This is the same mechanism used for RESV messages that arrive at the wrong router or interface.

The key remaining question is when to set up a short-cut for a QoS flow. Implementations SHOULD simply follow best effort traffic: if a best effort short-cut exists to a destination or next hop, the same endpoint SHOULD be used for RSVP-triggered QoS VCs. If best effort short-cuts are never established, QoS short-cuts will never be established either.
sections.eli5: A short-cut is a secret tunnel between two far-apart places. The rule is: use the tunnel for special traffic only if the normal traffic already uses it.

sections.title: Heterogeneous Multicast Sessions
sections.content:
Heterogeneous sessions occur only in multicast RSVP sessions, when receivers request different QoS levels or when some receivers request none. The framework in RFC 2382 offers four models: full heterogeneity, limited heterogeneity, homogeneous, and modified homogeneous. The goal is to deliver the requested QoS downstream, using one model or a combination.

No single model suits every case. The memo expects the limited or a hybrid limited-full model to be preferred in some networks such as public WANs, and the modified homogeneous model in others such as LANs. It therefore says implementations SHOULD implement one of the limited heterogeneity model or the modified homogeneous model. They SHOULD support both and let the user select, but are not required to.
sections.eli5: When many friends watch one show and some want HD while others are fine with normal, there are several ways to share. Pick at least one of the two suggested ways.

sections.title: Security
sections.content: The security considerations section is two sentences long. The same considerations stated in RFC 2205 (RSVP) and RFC 1755 (ATM signalling support for IP over ATM) apply, and the memo raises no additional security issues.
sections.eli5: It adds no new safety worries beyond the ones already known for RSVP and ATM.

items.title: Control messages
items.text: Send RSVP messages over the best effort data path.

items.title: VCs per reservation
items.text: Use independent VCs for each RSVP reservation.

items.title: Short-cuts
items.text: Follow best effort short-cuts for QoS flows.

items.title: Heterogeneity
items.text: Implement limited heterogeneity or modified homogeneous.
